editorial.thesis: A trading-and-motor-trade city of about 1.1 million. Its retail is heavy on cafés, tea & coffee and apparel, footwear & jewellery, and thin on desserts, sweets & ice cream and fitness & wellness — and 29% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 65% of Bhopal's. 7.05 chain outlets per lakh residents against 10.87 in Bhopal; 29 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Domino's 10, Bata 8, Raymond 6.

The mapped economy leans to malls & department stores. Shares of all mapped places: malls & department stores 0.7% (Bhopal 0.5%); shops & retail 16.5% (Bhopal 13.6%); leisure & entertainment 2.6% (Bhopal 3.4%); desserts & sweets 0.5% (Bhopal 0.7%). Raw counts would mislead because Bhopal is mapped more completely (16,390 places against 6,345), so we compare mix, not counts.

Supply and demand are misaligned. 4 zones hold 29% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Anand Nagar · Adhartal alone has about 116,000 residents and 19 mapped food & drink places.

Retail is less concentrated than in Bhopal. 51% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Bhopal 51%). The largest cores are Garha Phatak · Ganjipura (1,787 places) and Napier Town · Howbagh (1,570).

The widest brand gaps against Bhopal. Café Coffee Day 3 outlets vs 19; Domino's 10 outlets vs 25; Raymond 6 outlets vs 17. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 8 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Bhopal, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Napier Town · Howbagh and Garha Phatak · Ganjipura are the largest zones by residents (365,000 and 361,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 51% of all commercial places, and Garha Phatak · Ganjipura alone lists 1,787.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Napier Town · Howbagh holds 27 of the 81 tracked chain outlets, and Garha Phatak · Ganjipura adds 26.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Garha Phatak · Ganjipura and Napier Town · Howbagh lead on education places (253 and 217, with 91 and 60 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Anand Nagar · Adhartal and Garha Bazar. The blue cores include Garha Phatak · Ganjipura.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (16,390 places in Bhopal against 6,345 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Bhopal; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Bhopal, Jabalpur's mapped places over-index on malls & department stores (0.7% vs 0.5%), shops & retail (16.5% vs 13.6%), automotive (3.7% vs 3.4%) and under-index on leisure & entertainment (2.6% vs 3.4%), desserts & sweets (0.5% vs 0.7%), hotels & stays (6.0% vs 7.0%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 81 outlets of 29 tracked national brands within 8 km — 7.05 per lakh residents against Bhopal's 10.87 (193 outlets of 34 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Bhopal are Café Coffee Day (3 vs 19); Domino's (10 vs 25); Raymond (6 vs 17). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Bhopal's, so low means thin by Bhopal's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 8 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Jabalpur's age mix against Bhopal: children (0–14) 24.3% vs 26.0%, 15–24 20.1% vs 21.1%, working age 47.4% vs 45.5%, 60+ 8.2% vs 7.4%. Under-25s are 44% of residents.

zones.482001: Reasonably supplied: 1,570 places for about 365,000 residents (index 107), 27 chain outlets.
zones.482002: Reasonably supplied: 1,787 places for about 361,000 residents (index 123), 26 chain outlets.
zones.482004: An under-served zone: about 116,000 residents, 164 mapped places, 19 food & drink and 2 chain outlets. Depth index 35.
zones.482003: An under-served zone: about 111,000 residents, 240 mapped places, 28 food & drink and 1 chain outlet. Depth index 54.
zones.482008: An under-served zone: about 55,000 residents, 112 mapped places, 16 food & drink and 13 chain outlets. Depth index 51.
zones.482005: An under-served zone: about 38,000 residents, 76 mapped places, 3 food & drink and 0 chain outlets. Depth index 49.
zones.482009: A student-and-family belt: 8 education places (0 coaching) and 3 healthcare places for about 31,000 residents, with 2 food & drink places and 0 chain outlets.
zones.482020: A student-and-family belt: 21 education places (9 coaching) and 3 healthcare places for about 28,000 residents, with 8 food & drink places and 3 chain outlets.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 4.8% of mapped places against 5.0% in Bhopal, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 10 (Bhopal 25), Pizza Hut 4 (Bhopal 7), KFC 2 (Bhopal 7), Subway 2 (Bhopal 5). No mapped outlet in either city: Biryani By Kilo.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 3.1% of mapped places against 2.6% in Bhopal — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 3 (Bhopal 19), Chai Sutta Bar 2 (Bhopal 0). No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Point, Blue Tokai, Third Wave Coffee.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 0.5% of mapped places against 0.7% in Bhopal — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 5 (Bhopal 6). No mapped outlet in either city: Theobroma, Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.5% of mapped places against 1.4% in Bhopal, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 2 (Bhopal 9), Big Bazaar 2 (Bhopal 1), Vishal Mega Mart 2 (Bhopal 2), DMart 1 (Bhopal 2). No mapped outlet in either city: More, Easyday, Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.3% of mapped places against 1.5% in Bhopal — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Apollo Pharmacy, MedPlus, Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 6.1% of mapped places against 5.3% in Bhopal — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 8 (Bhopal 11), Raymond 6 (Bhopal 17), Tanishq 6 (Bhopal 4), Reliance Trends 5 (Bhopal 8).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 8.0% of mapped places against 7.7% in Bhopal, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.7% of mapped places against 3.9% in Bhopal, so the mix is level.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.6% of mapped places against 4.3% in Bhopal — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
